leads.title: MBT Enhanced Loading Systems
leads.uiStatement: Increases primary weapon rate of fire and improves secondary weapon heat recovery. Only active when countermeasures are not on cooldown.
leads.researchQuestion: Find the exact countermeasure-ready condition, affected primary and secondary owners, rate-of-fire and heat-recovery modifiers, and transition when cooldown begins or ends. Do not substitute reload speed for either effect.

leads.title: AA Enhanced Loading Systems
leads.uiStatement: Increases reload speed on both primary and secondary weapons. System deactivates when vehicle countermeasures are used.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace both reload receivers, countermeasure-use deactivation, and reactivation condition. Compare with VS01 only after exact identity is known; its UI description differs.

leads.title: IFV Systems Upgrade
leads.uiStatement: Faster cooldowns on equipment in slot 1; increased range and duration on equipment in slot 2.
leads.researchQuestion: Resolve Equipment 1 and Equipment 2 separately. Trace cooldown, range, and duration receivers for each compatible option; do not apply one modifier to all equipment.

leads.title: AA Systems Upgrade
leads.uiStatement: Faster cooldowns on all equipment and increased radar range.
leads.researchQuestion: Find equipment cooldown scope and the radar-range receiver. Determine whether the fixed Radar System supplies the radar owner. Do not transfer the IFV description.

leads.title: Emergency Repair and its health gate
leads.uiStatement: ATP, Attack Helicopter, IFV, MBT, and AA selection screens say damaged vehicles can be repaired only in a low-health state.
leads.researchQuestion: For each vehicle, trace the low-health threshold, activation predicate, repaired health owner, amount/rate, duration, charges, and cooldown. The Transport Helicopter overview also shows Emergency Repair, but supplies no description.

leads.title: Emergency Countermeasures and its health gate
leads.uiStatement: IFV and MBT: substantially improves countermeasure recharge rate at low health.
leads.researchQuestion: Find the health threshold, exact countermeasure owner, recharge operation, and recovery when health rises. Keep this distinct from Emergency Repair and Enhanced Loading.

leads.title: Field Maintenance
leads.uiStatement: IFV and MBT: faster vehicle health recovery after taking damage; also gains ammunition faster.
leads.researchQuestion: Separate health recovery delay/rate from ammunition replenishment delay/rate. Identify both receivers and the applicable damage-state conditions.

leads.title: ATP Integrated Medbay
leads.uiStatement: Increases health regeneration of friendly soldiers within a radius. Remains active after all soldiers exit if they remain nearby.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace team filter, radius, regeneration modifier, vehicle ownership, empty-vehicle persistence, distance cutoff, and shutdown on destruction or ownership change.

leads.title: ATP Combat Awareness System
leads.uiStatement: Hostiles remain spotted longer when they damage the vehicle or the owner's squadmates near it. Remains active after all soldiers exit but remain nearby.
leads.researchQuestion: Find damage-event inputs, owner/squad filters, distance test, spotting duration, and empty-vehicle persistence. Distinguish vehicle damage from damage to a nearby squadmate.

leads.title: Mobile Command Station: ATP versus IFV
leads.uiStatement: Both increase capture rate while inside an objective's capture area. ATP explicitly says the effect remains active after everyone exits but remains nearby; the IFV description does not state that extension.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace capture-volume condition and contribution operation. Test the ATP occupancy/proximity condition as a separate source question; do not infer IFV persistence from its omitted wording.

leads.title: Attack Helicopter Heavy Warheads
leads.uiStatement: Increases the blast radius lethality of primary weapon payloads and ammunition capacity. Diminishes aircraft maneuverability.
leads.researchQuestion: Find primary-only scope, blast-related modifiers, capacity receiver, and maneuverability penalty. The phrase blast radius lethality does not identify a particular radius/damage field or equation.

leads.title: Attack Helicopter Thermal Optics crosses seats
leads.uiStatement: Located in Driver / Upgrade, but the description enables thermal vision for the attack helicopter gunner while zoomed.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace driver-selected equipment to the gunner camera/optic receiver and zoom predicate. This is a useful control against assuming that the selecting seat receives the effect.

leads.title: Helicopter Targeting Interference and speed gate
leads.uiStatement: Slows enemy lock acquisition and clears the aircraft spotted marker sooner. Deactivates if the aircraft travels too slowly.
leads.researchQuestion: Find speed threshold and units, lock and spotting receivers, activation hysteresis, and differences between Attack and Scout Helicopter owners.

leads.title: Attack Helicopter Target Detection System
leads.uiStatement: Tracks and identifies enemy infantry and vehicles. The attack helicopter is more vulnerable to lock-on weapons while active.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace detection targets/radius/duration and the simultaneous lock-vulnerability penalty; identify activation and shutdown conditions.

leads.title: Optimized Handling
leads.uiStatement: Improves vehicle turning rate and aiming speed.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace chassis turning and aiming/turret receivers separately for MBT and AA; establish the operation and units before reporting an effective speed.

leads.title: Scout Helicopter Emergency Stabilizer
leads.uiStatement: Reduces the effect of mobility hits, making the vehicle easier to control.
leads.researchQuestion: Target the mobility-hit response, severity/duration and affected controls. Do not assume a normal-flight handling bonus.

leads.title: Scout Helicopter Engine Upgrade
leads.uiStatement: Faster acceleration and top speed at the cost of maneuverability.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace acceleration, speed limit, and maneuverability receivers as three separate effects; identify the source operation for each.

leads.title: Ground Targeting Jammer
leads.uiStatement: Slows lock acquisition, clears the spotted marker sooner, and reduces heat signature in thermal imaging.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace lock, spotting, and thermal-visibility receivers independently. Do not import the helicopter speed gate unless an exact chain establishes it.

leads.title: MBT Projectile Intercept System
leads.uiStatement: Intercepts enemy missiles, shells, rockets, grenades, and bombs. Intercepts all projectiles during an activation window that starts after initial detection.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace projectile-class/team filters, detection trigger, window timer, capacity, and cooldown. The word all is a UI claim, not a proved unlimited capacity or universal filter.

leads.title: ATP Grenade Intercept System
leads.uiStatement: Tracks and destroys projectiles such as hand-thrown and launched grenades. Can intercept up to three during an activation window after initial detection.
leads.researchQuestion: Find the three-intercept counter, allowed projectile classes, detection/window timing, reset and cooldown. Compare with MBT protection without merging the two systems.

leads.title: Gunner Mine Countermeasures
leads.uiStatement: Detects mines and C-4, enabling the operator to activate countermeasures to destroy them.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace detection, mine/C-4 eligibility, manual activation, destruction, radius, and charges/cooldown. IFV overview also shows Countermeasures, but has no selection description in this collection.

leads.title: Thermal-Blocking Smoke damage and guidance effects
leads.uiStatement: IFV, MBT, and AA: obscures the vehicle, disrupts incoming lock-on missile guidance, blocks spotting, and deals moderate damage to enemy infantry in the smoke radius.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace smoke lifetime/radius, missile-guidance disruption, spotting control, and the enemy-infantry damage channel. Patrol Boat has an overview label only; do not transfer values to it.

leads.title: Smoke Generator, Smoke Wall Launcher, and Scout Smoke Launcher
leads.uiStatement: ATP/IFV Smoke Generator emits continuously and can lay a wall while driving. ATP/MBT Smoke Wall Launcher fires multiple projectiles. Scout Smoke Launcher fires multiple grenades to form a cloud. Each says it blocks spotting and clears spotted markers from all infantry in the smoke radius.
leads.researchQuestion: Separate emitter, projectile, and grenade deployment. Trace lifetime, radius, marker clearing and team scope; all infantry must not silently become friendly-only. These descriptions do not state the thermal-smoke damage effect.

leads.title: IFV Proximity Threat Detector
leads.uiStatement: Detects nearby enemy soldiers and vehicles and shows them on the minimap for a short duration.
leads.researchQuestion: Find target filters, detection radius, refresh cadence, display duration, and recipients.

leads.title: IFV Counter-Fire Radar
leads.uiStatement: Passively spots sources of incoming damage. Can be activated to extend spotting and designate spotted enemy vehicles.
leads.researchQuestion: Separate passive damage-source spotting from active extension/designation. Trace target type, recipients, timers, and designation consumers.

leads.title: Scout dropped Motion Sensor
leads.uiStatement: Dropped device embeds in the ground and shows nearby moving enemies, vehicles, and gadgets on team minimaps. Infantry can avoid detection while moving crouched or prone. Emits a sound audible to hostiles.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace dropped-device lifecycle, ground placement, movement/stance and type filters, radius, team-wide recipients, duration, and sound event. Compare infantry sensor logic only after exact ownership is known.

leads.title: Scout Tactical Data System
leads.uiStatement: Enemies spotted by the Scout Helicopter's equipment and radar receive world and minimap markers for all team members, not only the user's squad.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace radar/equipment input scope and squad-to-team recipient change; distinguish world markers from minimap markers and ordinary designation.

leads.title: Scout Target Designator
leads.uiStatement: Marks vehicles and locations. Designated targets can be locked from farther away and lose below-radar protection.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace designation token, vehicle/location distinction, target lifetime, compatible lock receivers, extended range, and below-radar override.

leads.title: Directional Jammer: Scout and Multirole Jet
leads.uiStatement: Targets enemy handheld and vehicle-mounted devices to prevent lock-on against the equipped aircraft or other vehicles. Extended use temporarily overheats it.
leads.researchQuestion: Find directional/line-of-sight and range tests, affected devices and protected targets, heat accumulation, overheat cutoff and recovery. Preserve separate owners for Scout and Jet.

leads.title: MBT five ammunition options and duplicate exclusion
leads.uiStatement: Both Primary and Alternate Ammo show Multi-Purpose HE (120 mm HEAT-MP-T: infantry and armor), Armor-Piercing (120 mm APFSDS: heavy armor, no explosive charge), Anti-Personnel (120 mm canister: short/medium infantry use, ineffective against armor), High Explosive (120 mm HEMP-T: large fragmentation radius, less effective against armor), and Aim-Guided (120 mm guided munition: anti-vehicle crosshair guidance). Primary shows Aim-Guided blocked as already equipped elsewhere; Alternate Ammo shows Multi-Purpose blocked.
leads.researchQuestion: Reuse the L3254 exact five-option condition chains. Trace which slot selects which condition, duplicate exclusion, switching, ammunition ownership, and each projectile channel. UI order is not factory default order.

leads.title: IFV three primary shell types
leads.uiStatement: High Explosive / HEI-T targets infantry and unarmored vehicles, less effective against armor. Anti-Personnel / canister targets infantry at short/medium range and is ineffective against armor. Armor-Piercing / APDS targets heavy armor with no explosive charge and lower infantry effectiveness.
leads.researchQuestion: Resolve exact primary alternatives and projectiles. Compare direct/blast/canister channels, target multipliers and cadence without treating qualitative UI wording as numbers.

leads.title: AA three primary shell types
leads.uiStatement: 35 mm AAMP is anti-air and ineffective against armored ground vehicles. 35 mm AAHV is quick-firing for fast/light aircraft. 35 mm AAAP is slow-firing with high damage against armored targets and best against slow aircraft, yet also states ineffective against armored ground vehicles.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace fire cadence, projectile speed, air/ground target filters and armor multipliers. Preserve the distinction between armored aircraft and armored ground vehicles; the Anti-Armor label alone is misleading.

leads.title: Coax and RWS LMG/HMG/AGL ownership
leads.uiStatement: 7.62 mm LMG descriptions favor medium-range infantry and are less effective against light armor. .50 cal HMG favors long-range infantry and unarmored vehicles. RWS 40 mm AGL favors close-range infantry and unarmored targets. MBT lists HMG before LMG in the gunner menu; ATP/IFV list LMG first.
leads.researchQuestion: Use L3303/L3304 exact caller and RWS AGL evidence to map each UI option to its distinct firing owner. Keep coax, RWS, stationary and SP owners separate; investigate reload, heat, replenishment and damage composition only through controlled receivers.

leads.title: Scout primary gun alternatives
leads.uiStatement: 7.62 mm Minigun: rapid fire for infantry and lightly armored vehicles. 40 mm AGL: close-range infantry and unarmored targets. .50 cal Heavy Rotary MG: long-range infantry and unarmored vehicles.
leads.researchQuestion: Resolve each Scout primary owner and projectile. Compare cadence, heat, replenishment and damage channels. Do not reuse RWS AGL/HMG values based on name or caliber.

leads.title: Patrol Boat primary alternatives and suspect cannon description
leads.uiStatement: .50 cal Heavy Rotary MG favors long-range infantry and unarmored vehicles. The 30 mm Cannon text literally calls it a helicopter-mounted fully automatic cannon effective against most targets, including tanks, although this is a Patrol Boat screen.
leads.researchQuestion: Resolve the exact boat cannon and rotary-gun owners. Check whether the helicopter wording is shared/stale metadata; it does not prove shared gameplay assets or equivalent damage.

leads.title: Light and heavy unguided rockets
leads.uiStatement: Attack/Scout 70 mm FFAR Light Rockets: larger volleys with lower damage per projectile, suited to light vehicles and infantry. Attack 127 mm FFAR and Jet Heavy Rockets: smaller volleys with higher damage per projectile, including armored targets. IFV 127 mm Rockets says unguided and effective against almost all targets.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace volley count, capacity, cadence, replenishment, projectile direct/blast channels, and vehicle-specific owners. Do not infer the IFV uses the same heavy-rocket values.

leads.title: Aim-Guided 70 mm rockets
leads.uiStatement: 70 mm PGM rockets for infantry and light vehicles; guided via weapon crosshairs.
leads.researchQuestion: Find guidance input, turn limits, projectile lifetime, compatible firing owners and damage channels; distinguish rockets from the missiles and shells with the same short label.

leads.title: Attack Helicopter secondary missiles
leads.uiStatement: ALM-93 Lock-Guided: anti-air, prelaunch lock then self-guidance unless intercepted; faster and longer-range lock on Laser Designator/Tracer Dart targets. M41A7 TOW2 Aim-Guided: anti-tank crosshair guidance, also capable of locking designated/traced targets.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace guidance mode selection, designation/Tracer Dart consumers, lock time/range, countermeasure response and target filters for each exact missile.

leads.title: IFV secondary guided missiles
leads.uiStatement: M41A7 TOW2 Aim-Guided says anti-vehicle crosshair guidance. MR Missile Lock-Guided says prelaunch lock, self-guidance, countermeasure vulnerability, and faster/longer locks on Laser Designator/Tracer Dart targets. The IFV TOW description omits the Attack Helicopter lock-on statement.
leads.researchQuestion: Resolve each exact missile owner and mode. Check designation support through source evidence rather than either assuming it from the shared TOW label or treating omitted UI wording as proof of absence.

leads.title: AA secondary missile variants
leads.uiStatement: SLM-93A SPIRE Lock-Guided: anti-air prelaunch lock, self-guidance, countermeasure vulnerability; designation increases range and removes below-radar protection. SKR-70 Aim-Guided: maneuverable laser-guided missile aimed by crosshair, described as able to bypass countermeasures. R-84E High Velocity: larger aircraft, limited point-of-aim guidance, trades maneuverability for speed.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace each guidance model, target filters, speed/turn parameters, designation and below-radar conditions, and countermeasure response. Do not equate High Velocity UI wording with a named serialized field.

leads.title: Patrol Boat secondary AA missile variants
leads.uiStatement: SKR-70 Aim-Guided: beam-riding, then pilots itself after manual guidance; immune to flares during manual guidance but vulnerable to countermeasures afterwards. SIROCCO 4 Lock-Guided: prelaunch lock then self-guidance; designation increases range and removes below-radar protection.
leads.researchQuestion: Prioritize the SKR-70 manual-to-autonomous transition and phase-specific flare response. Compare with AA SKR-70 only through exact identities; its UI description is different.

leads.title: Multirole API versus APHEI cannon
leads.uiStatement: 20 mm API: Armor Piercing Incendiary, best against aircraft and light vehicles. 20 mm APHEI: Armor-Piercing High-Explosive Incendiary, effective against most targets but lower muzzle velocity makes fast targets harder to engage.
leads.researchQuestion: Reopen L3033 only with a new exact text/selection-to-weapon link. Resolve projectile identity, speed and direct/blast channels. Screenshot availability does not prove a carrier/map restriction or unrestricted availability.

leads.title: Multirole Lock-Guided AA missile
leads.uiStatement: AIM-84 air-to-air missile: locks on or utilizes laser guidance to target any aircraft.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace lock/laser mode selection, designation receiver and aircraft eligibility. Do not infer the same behavior as other Lock-Guided labels.

leads.title: Multirole Auto-Guided AA missile
leads.uiStatement: HAM-88 anti-radiation missile homes on vehicles with anti-air missile systems. Damage temporarily jams struck targets. Effective against surface targets and slow aircraft.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace anti-radiation eligibility, acquisition, homing, on-hit jamming, duration and recovery. Keep physical damage and temporary disabling effects separate.

leads.title: Multirole gunner Active-Lock AA missile
leads.uiStatement: ARH-7 air-to-air missile requires the user to maintain sight lock until impact.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace sustained-lock ownership, loss-of-sight behavior, guidance termination/reacquisition and gunner control. Do not derive fire-and-forget behavior from the ARH label.

leads.title: Multirole Anti-Armor Cluster Bomb
leads.uiStatement: Dispenses numerous anti-armor submunitions over a target location.
leads.researchQuestion: Find parent/child projectile identities, release count/spread, activation height/timing, target eligibility, and per-submunition versus total damage composition.

leads.title: Multirole gunner Bomb
leads.uiStatement: 230 kg PGM guides itself to the targeting crosshair point at release and can penetrate subsurface structures.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace release-time target sampling, subsequent guidance, collision/penetration and detonation. Do not assume continuous crosshair following.

leads.title: Multirole gunner Optical Missile
leads.uiStatement: AGM-2000H/K precision munition controlled through an optical feed, allowing mid-flight adjustment; primarily for armored ground targets, with other stated uses against structures, infantry and aircraft.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace camera/control handoff, mid-flight steering, lifetime/range, interruption conditions, projectile channels and target eligibility.

leads.title: Patrol Boat Torpedo
leads.uiStatement: Stern-launched wire-guided torpedo capable of very high damage to enemy watercraft.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace launch transform, water movement, control input, guidance limits, target collision filter, lifetime and damage receiver.

leads.title: Patrol Boat Naval Mine
leads.uiStatement: Waterborne mine detonates on contact with watercraft.
leads.researchQuestion: Find deployment, arming, watercraft/contact and team filters, persistence and explosion receiver. Respect the L3303 alternate-schema limit; do not read it as an ordinary bullet without a control.

leads.title: Patrol Boat mortar options and two gunner slots
leads.uiStatement: Overview shows one Gunner Remote Weapon slot with High Explosive and a second with IR Smoke. The second slot selection has IR Smoke Shell (obscures vision), HE Guided / 120 mm HEGM (locks Laser Designator/Tracer Dart targets), Airburst / 120 mm Mortar AB (bursts near aircraft, boats or ground), and Illumination / 120 mm Mortar ILL (parachute flare marks enemies below).
leads.researchQuestion: Use L3303 five mortar paths as candidates, not UI joins. Resolve the two slots, fixed HE versus selectable second slot, smoke effect, designated guidance, proximity fuze target/ground tests, and illumination spotting/lifetime. Four selectable choices plus a displayed HE slot are not evidence that a fifth option is missing.

leads.title: Seat counts, role labels and source station controls
leads.uiStatement: UI seat counts: ATP 4; Attack Helicopter 2; Attack Jet 1; Fighter Jet 1; IFV 6; Interceptor Jet 2; Light Ground Transport 5; MBT 2; AA 1; Multirole Jet 2; Patrol Boat 2; Scout Helicopter 4; Transport Helicopter 5. Customization shows weapon/equipment roles, not every passenger seat.
leads.researchQuestion: Compare UI category/seat roles with L3100-L3112 and L3250-L3257 exact source stations. Use UH-60 left/right miniguns, Attack Helicopter gunner, MBT coax and Light Transport gunner as controls. UI seat count is attributed text, not a universal count across variants/modes.

leads.title: UI slot identity, fixed entries and captured selections
leads.uiStatement: Screens separate Driver/Gunner roles, equipment slots, inspected versus equipped cards, locked items, and already-equipped-in-another-slot restrictions. Multiple Remote Weapon and Upgrade labels occur in one vehicle. Loadout 1 is selected in the captured overview screens.
leads.researchQuestion: Match exact UI producer/slot IDs to equipment and source receivers. Preserve slot ordinal and seat. A grey card is a displayed state, not proof of an unusable seat or absent effect. Saved player Loadout 1 is not a factory default. Use the duplicate-exclusion control before generalizing it.

leads.title: Build, faction, category and recipe applicability
leads.uiStatement: Screens show vehicle categories and a Swap Faction control. Capture filenames in the prior rename manifest are dated 3 October 2026; the images do not identify archive Head or descriptor hash.
leads.researchQuestion: Establish the captured client/build and faction/variant context before claiming source equivalence or an update delta. Test exact category-to-root and root-to-recipe selection only with a new typed selector. Keep standard multiplayer, campaign, AI and Granite variants separate.

leads.title: Fixed/overview-only equipment and missing descriptions
leads.uiStatement: Overview-only labels include Flares, Radar System, firing-port weapons, gunner Cannon and Lock-Guided, Thermal Scanner, Sweep Stance, Deploy Ramp, Improved Armor, fixed jet loadouts, and Transport Helicopter Emergency Repair/miniguns. Attack Helicopter Improved Armor selection separately says resistance against most infantry weapons.
leads.researchQuestion: Find descriptions/owners for these exact slots using existing metadata before any small missing capture. Trace flare/lock-break timing, radar/scanner filters, Sweep Stance selection and armor resistance as separate questions. Do not borrow descriptions from another vehicle or treat missing selection screenshots as proof that an item cannot be selected.

leads.title: Visible mastery unlock requirements
leads.uiStatement: Visible locked cards state mastery thresholds; unlocked cards generally show Select or Equipped instead of the original requirement. These are captured account/UI states.
leads.researchQuestion: If progression is in scope, map exact unlock rules and family IDs. Do not reconstruct missing requirements from card order. Keep this optional after functional leads; ask for additional evidence only if necessary.

leads.title: Patrol Boat Deploy Ramp and spawn condition
leads.uiStatement: Category description says the boat can act as a deploy point when its front ramp is lowered on shore. Overview shows Driver / Upgrade: Deploy Ramp.
leads.researchQuestion: Trace ramp state, on-shore/grounding condition, spawn eligibility and team/squad permissions. Do not infer this behavior from boat presence alone.

leads.title: Category protection tags and actual protection
leads.uiStatement: Category tags include Shielded Seats (ATP, AA), Open Seats (Light Transport), Hard Target (MBT), and Soft Target (jets). ATP description mentions mine blast protection. Attack Helicopter Improved Armor says resistance against most infantry weapons.
leads.researchQuestion: Treat these as UI claims. For useful comparisons, trace occupant protection, mine/blast handling and infantry-weapon armor filters through exact health/damage owners. Tags do not establish damage multipliers or directional armor.
